title: §5 attribution — no stack member accounts for the substitute/counter regression
method: ablate one policy-side cell at a time on 4000 frozen on-distribution decisions; report pick_rate (P(argmax==mechanic)) and mean_prob among decisions where the mechanic was LEGAL. Within-sample contrast, so the arms are directly comparable.
verdict: NEITHER v84 nor v85 is implicated. Ablating intent_threshold changes nothing; ablating intent_conditional moves counter +0.005 and substitute -0.001 — inside noise and in the WRONG direction to explain a regression (removing a cell does not RESTORE the mechanic).
scope_limit_stated_plainly: This tested the v84/v85 CELLS, because §5's mechanics are theirs. It did NOT test the three RIDERS whose unconditionalization decision-5 gates (--op-drop-renders, --op-believed-lean, --item-belief). D therefore exonerates the cells and says NOTHING about the riders; the gate is not satisfied by this result.
caveats: the h/r family arms (the work order's 'if cheap' option) were NOT run — adding edge-family ablation to this probe was not cheap
the sample is the forensically-captured subset, not §5's full trace population, so the LEVELS here are not comparable to §5's numbers; only the cross-arm contrast is
a defect was found and fixed mid-run (an all-ones action mask); the fix changed nothing to 4 decimals because the pointer head derives legality from the obs itself
